root_cause: The Windows CC (conditional compilation collect mode) build runs many parallel ninja link jobs on a memory-constrained Windows runner. MSVC's link.exe for several small sample executables fails with LNK1102 (out of memory) when too many link/compile jobs run concurrently and exhaust available RAM, not because of any code defect. This is the same recurring infrastructure signature observed 21 times since 2026-11-03, unrelated to the PR's content (an NPU VCL loader refactor) which does not touch the Windows samples build.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI; it depends on runner memory pressure and ninja parallelism. Locally, building the full Release tree with CC enabled and a high ninja job count (-j matching or exceeding available cores) on a memory-limited Windows machine can reproduce LNK1102.
recommended_actions: Reduce ninja/link parallelism (-j) for the Windows CC build job or set CMAKE_JOB_POOLS to cap concurrent link jobs.
Increase the Windows runner's available memory/swap or move the CC collect-mode job to a larger runner SKU.
Investigate using /INCREMENTAL or splitting link steps to lower peak linker memory usage for the samples subset.
Since this pattern has recurred 21 times, escalate to CI infra owners to adjust the Windows_Conditional_Compilation workflow's parallelism/runner sizing rather than re-investigating case by case.
prevention_strategies: Cap the number of concurrent MSVC link jobs via CMake job pools (e.g., JOB_POOLS link=2) specifically for Release/CC builds on Windows runners, and monitor runner memory usage in this workflow to catch OOM conditions before linking many binaries in parallel.
historical_context: This exact signature (compiler/linker out-of-memory on Windows CC build) has been recorded 21 times in the pattern database since 2026-11-03T07:07:04Z, most recently at 2026-11-23T13:22:55Z, across many unrelated commits/PRs, confirming this is a persistent CI infrastructure issue rather than a code regression introduced by PR #39413.
